requirements.requirement: Serve the inventory application on node1 over TCP port 8181.
requirements.summary: Apache is active and listening on TCP/8181, and an HTTP request to node1's IP returns the inventory application. The same service, listener, and content recovered after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the system's mandatory access control in enforcing mode while serving the application.
requirements.summary: SELinux remained Enforcing, TCP/8181 was assigned to http_port_t, and the application operated successfully under that policy before and after restart, with no captured post-boot HTTPD AVC denials.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. The inventory application is reachable on TCP/8181 while SELinux remains enforcing. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and service, content, SELinux policy, firewall state, and listener recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The application request was made from node1 to its own node IP rather than from a separate external client, although the all-interface listener and active runtime/permanent firewall rule strongly support network availability.
The lifecycle snapshots do not directly inventory SELinux mode, firewall rules, application files, or installed packages; those final states are instead established by executor commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands had a clear task or restart-evidence purpose; no unrelated troubleshooting mutations were identified. Package installation, application/configuration creation, the SELinux port assignment, HTTPD enablement, firewall changes, and scheduled restart were justified. The transient restart unit was naturally removed by reboot. Hygiene is reduced because enabling the stock HTTPD configuration also retained an all-interface TCP/80 listener that was not needed for the requested TCP/8181 service; it remained after completion. This is attributable to the HTTPD installation/enablement actions rather than a separate unrelated command.
